scope: Gyurme Dorje 2001, printed pp308–316 (PDF309–317), historical divination of death

anchor.original_text_reference: White Beryl ff.343b–354a; Moonbeams ff.34a–36a; plates 11 and 19

source_notes.paraphrase: The source distinguishes prognostications about death grounded in living relatives, about the deceased, and a separate class of funeral-ceremony divination. These require different subjects and different observations.

anchor.original_text_reference: White Beryl ff.343b–354a; Moonbeams ff.34a–36a; plates 11 and 19

source_notes.paraphrase: For the living-relative calculation, a grid to the right on white felt represents living family members by sex and seniority. One year-animal pebble, four personal-force contrasts, one annual mewa, one annual trigram, five growth/decline, seven harshness and one natal mewa make 20 fixed pebbles per designated reading.

anchor.original_text_reference: White Beryl ff.343b–354a; Moonbeams ff.34a–36a; plates 11 and 19

source_notes.paraphrase: The described grid assigns colored/numbered pebbles to twelve year animals and the five elemental constitutions; marker identity and cardinality are part of the method, not observed frequencies of death.

anchor.original_text_reference: White Beryl ff.343b–354a; Moonbeams ff.34a–36a; plates 11 and 19

source_notes.paraphrase: A death-omen table compares the majority year signs of paternal relatives or other household members with each subject's fourth-removed and seventh-removed animal-sign aspects, attributing a classical conflict omen.

anchor.original_text_reference: White Beryl ff.343b–354a; Moonbeams ff.34a–36a; plates 11 and 19

source_notes.paraphrase: The source combines dominant elemental constitution/animal-year of paternal relatives with one or two minority animal-year relatives, producing conditional narratives about household and ancestral graves.

anchor.original_text_reference: White Beryl ff.343b–354a; Moonbeams ff.34a–36a; plates 11 and 19

source_notes.paraphrase: Plate11 fig4 distinguishes six majority groupings of natal mewa among paternal relatives (White1/6/8, Black2, Green4, Yellow5, Red7/9, Blue3), with different alleged causes and religious responses.

anchor.original_text_reference: White Beryl ff.343b–354a; Moonbeams ff.34a–36a; plates 11 and 19

source_notes.paraphrase: For paternal relatives the source treats a black vitality marker as a life-spirit issue, black body as illness, black destiny as resource loss and black luck as reputation-related conflict. Targets and outcome domains are distinct.

anchor.original_text_reference: White Beryl ff.343b–354a; Moonbeams ff.34a–36a; plates 11 and 19

source_notes.paraphrase: Plate11 fig5 classifies twelve pebbles of the life-spirit by five constitutional forms plus greater/lesser penalty and directional destiny/mother/son/friend/enemy year relations. These are symbolic relationships, not 12 independent mortality cases.

anchor.original_text_reference: White Beryl ff.343b–354a; Moonbeams ff.34a–36a; plates 11 and 19

source_notes.paraphrase: Moonbeams presents funeral divination using 199 pebbles and twelve classes including deceased vitality/body/destiny/luck/year element, trigram, numeric-square polarity, funeral type, corpse type, direction, rebirth-place and ritual closing. These are a post-death classification, not birth-only prediction.

anchor.original_text_reference: White Beryl ff.343b–354a; Moonbeams ff.34a–36a; plates 11 and 19

source_notes.paraphrase: The section on timely vs untimely death enumerates eight classifying aspects: vitality, body, destiny, luck, constitutional type, trigram, numeric square and animal year; they require a known deceased case and contextual data.

anchor.original_text_reference: White Beryl ff.343b–354a; Moonbeams ff.34a–36a; plates 11 and 19

source_notes.paraphrase: The White Beryl method describes 58 basic pebbles alongside recognition markers for a Fire Horse-year deceased, with its own exemplar chart. The exact complete marker count is not equivalent to the 20 living-family or 199 funeral pebbles.

anchor.original_text_reference: White Beryl ff.343b–354a; Moonbeams ff.34a–36a; plates 11 and 19

source_notes.paraphrase: For each of vitality, body, destiny and luck in the death context, the narrative largely treats a black conclusive pebble as timely/exhausted circumstances and a white one as untimely/disruption, reversing any simplistic good-white/bad-black rule.

anchor.original_text_reference: White Beryl ff.343b–354a; Moonbeams ff.34a–36a; plates 11 and 19

source_notes.paraphrase: Supplementary Plate19 fig3 has an eight-trigram table of animal-year categories associated with timely death (enemy trigram relations) versus untimely death (identity trigram relations); direct date/trigram convention is required.

anchor.original_text_reference: White Beryl ff.343b–354a; Moonbeams ff.34a–36a; plates 11 and 19

source_notes.paraphrase: Supplementary Plate19 fig4 uses concurrence of the four minor obstacle numeric squares with Black Two combinations as one condition in classifying timely death; absence of the precise mewa method cannot be treated as negative.

anchor.original_text_reference: White Beryl ff.343b–354a; Moonbeams ff.34a–36a; plates 11 and 19

source_notes.paraphrase: Supplementary Plate19 fig5 combines seven harsh aspects, natal-year return, fourth/seventh removed relations, multiple-of-nine and tomb signs along with year/month/day/hour; the conjunction is multi-input and not reducible to one birthday.

anchor.original_text_reference: White Beryl ff.343b–354a; Moonbeams ff.34a–36a; plates 11 and 19

source_notes.paraphrase: Supplementary Plate19 fig6 final tally describes a majority of black pebbles as timely death and majority white as untimely death. This is a post-event theological or historical judgment, not evidence of when a living person will die.

methodology: Distinguish living relatives vs deceased and funerary/cultural classification; no prognostic accuracy. Keep religious and symbolic rationale separate from scientific study.
ethical_boundary: Not medical, survival or funeral advice
No verified cases or untreated deaths known from these passages
Distinct base counts 20,58,199 and multiple families cannot be merged
